node.label: Dispositive Motion Filed Before Trial?
node.note: After claim construction and expert discovery, either side may move for summary judgment on infringement, invalidity, or (if liability is undisputed) damages. This feeds back into the SAME RCFC 56/58/59/54/EAJA machinery already modeled on the general track -- §1498's remedy limits (no injunction, no enhanced damages, no jury) constrain what any resulting judgment can award, but not the procedural mechanics of getting there.

options.label: Move for summary judgment on infringement, invalidity, or (if liability is undisputed) damages
options.note: Feeds back into the same RCFC 56/58/59/54/EAJA machinery already modeled on the general track.

options.label: No dispositive motion; proceed to a bench trial on damages ('reasonable and entire compensation') and any remaining liability issues
options.note: §1498(a) constrains the REMEDY (no injunction, no enhanced/treble damages, no jury) but not the procedural mechanics of reaching judgment.
